edits.replacement: The drainage decay half-life t½ = ln(2)/β₃ is the time for excess groundwater storage above the drainage datum to drain to half its initial value, an intuitive measure of aquifer memory that depends on the drainage rate alone (Table 7; Figure 14). The eastern open dune turns over rapidly (C1 median 7.0 months, C2 10.1), the western dune is intermediate (C3 median 13.2 months), and the forest interior shows the longest memory in the network (C4 median 29.8 months, individual wells to 88). C5 Coastal Forest (median 15.6 months) resembles the western dune despite sharing the pine canopy, reinforcing the substrate and elevation control. The half-life is a pure drainage-rate measure, whereas the storage-drainage index τ = Sy/β₃ additionally weights it by specific yield; because Sy and 1/β₃ are spatially independent across the network (r = 0.13), the two produce near-identical spatial patterns (r = 0.98) and the cluster ranking is unchanged. Plotted together with the SSM-over-TLM gain and specific yield as three independently derived descriptors (t½, ΔNSE, Sy), the five clusters occupy distinct, non-overlapping regions of diagnostic space (Figure 15) — a model-based characterization of aquifer architecture consistent with, but derived independently of, the Ward’s clustering.
